skill.name: etetoolkit
skill.description: Work with ETE Toolkit for phylogenetic tree manipulation, NCBI taxonomy annotation, orthology analysis, clustering, and publication-ready visualization.
skill.summary: Use ETE to manipulate, compare, annotate, and visualize phylogenetic trees.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, biological taxonomy lookups, and documented local output examples. Two sudo install instructions are confirmed because they request elevated system package changes for optional Qt rendering dependencies. No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo apt-get commands with manual-install guidance requiring explicit user approval, or link to official ETE dependency documentation.

remediation.issue: Large hidden taxonomy cache side effect
remediation.suggestion: Keep the cache path warning and recommend a user-selected dbfile or workspace cache when possible.

content.value_statement: Phylogenetic workflows often require careful tree parsing, annotation, comparison, and visualization. This skill guides ETE Toolkit usage with focused examples and helper scripts.
actual_capabilities: Explains ETE Tree, PhyloTree, ClusterTree, and NCBITaxa workflows.
Provides helper scripts for tree conversion, rooting, pruning, statistics, and ASCII output.
Provides a visualization script for PNG, PDF, and SVG tree rendering.
Documents NCBI taxonomy lookup, lineage retrieval, and species tree construction.
Shows workflows for ortholog detection, tree comparison, clustering, and batch processing.
limitations: Requires ETE3 and optional Qt packages for rendering or GUI features.
NCBI taxonomy use can download a large local database on first run.
Examples assume valid Newick, FASTA, Phylip, or matrix input files.
The skill does not replace biological review of evolutionary interpretations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Trees for Analysis
use_cases.description: Convert formats, reroot trees, prune taxa, and generate basic statistics before downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Annotate Species Context
use_cases.description: Use NCBI taxonomy workflows to map names, retrieve lineages, and build species trees.

use_cases.title: Create Publication Figures
use_cases.description: Style tree layouts, show branch support, and render visual outputs for reports or manuscripts.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Tree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a Newick file
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the etetoolkit skill to inspect my Newick tree. Report leaf count, total nodes, branch length range, and any parsing concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Analysis Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the etetoolkit skill to plan commands for midpoint rooting, pruning to my focal taxa, and writing a clean Newick output.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate Taxonomy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the etetoolkit skill to design an NCBI taxonomy annotation workflow for my species tree and explain the cache behavior first.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Gene Trees
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the etetoolkit skill to compare several gene trees, report Robinson-Foulds distances, and propose visualization choices for conflicting clades.

output: A workflow for name translation, lineage lookup, and node feature annotation.

output_examples.input: A manuscript needs a styled phylogenetic figure.
output: A rendering plan with layout mode, support labels, and vector output.
A description of optional Qt requirements.
A short review checklist for publication readiness.

best_practices: Confirm Newick format settings before reading or writing trees.
Use iterators and cached content for large trees to reduce memory use.
Explain NCBI cache downloads before running taxonomy workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged package installation without explicit user approval.
Do not assume gene names map cleanly to species names without validation.
Do not overwrite original tree files before checking converted outputs.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps use ETE Toolkit for phylogenetic tree manipulation, taxonomy annotation, analysis, comparison, and visualization.

faq.question: Does it include executable scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes helper scripts for tree operations and quick visualization using local input and output files.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: NCBI taxonomy workflows can trigger a large taxonomy database download on first use.

faq.question: Can it produce publication figures?
faq.answer: Yes. The visualization guidance covers PNG, PDF, and SVG output with layout and node styling options.

faq.question: Can it identify orthologs?
faq.answer: It documents PhyloTree workflows for duplication, speciation, orthology, and paralogy analysis.

faq.question: Is biological interpretation automated?
faq.answer: No. The skill supports analysis workflows, but domain experts should review evolutionary conclusions.
